name: Shit Brown
lede: Shit Brown is a dark yellowish brown that entered our color list through a 2010 online naming survey, and its blunt name is a fair summary of how brown is often treated.

sections.title: A crowd's name
sections.body:
The name comes from the xkcd color survey of 2010, in which thousands of people typed their own names for screen colors [1]. It has no earlier record in our sources, and no book we hold uses it as a color term [1]. In the ISCC-NBS system the swatch is nearest to "moderate olive brown", at a CIEDE2000 distance of 4.3 [1].

The bluntness is not new in spirit. St Clair writes that brown is the color of the earth we return to, and also of mud and worse, and that part of its bad reputation is that it is a shade, not a hue [2]. You will not find it in the rainbow or on a simple color wheel [2]; in her account it has to be made by dulling and darkening warm colors or by mixing the artists' primaries [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
The color itself is common in painting. It appears in 523 of 23,781 paintings in our archive, 2.2 per cent, more often than 75 per cent of the named colors [3]. It peaks in the 1800s, in 1.3 per cent of the 8,345 paintings from that century [3]. In 45 per cent of the 274 paintings where the within-painting lens finds it, it plays an accent [3].

The earliest match is dated 1299, 711 years before the name was recorded, and the archive's early centuries are thin [3]. It shares canvases with [[pinchbeck-brown]] more than chance would predict [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a match is a look-alike hue and not proof of a pigment [3].

openers: Brown is not in the rainbow: you have to darken and gray a yellow or orange to make it.
This name has no record before a 2010 online survey.

issues: Reworded St Clair passage that followed her phrasing too closely.
